page.title: WearMask: Face Mask Detection | Real-time, In-browser AI
page.description: A free face mask detector. Just a tablet, you can get a mask detection AI! Designed for small businesses and public places, let us defeat COVID-19 together.

tips.message: Fully cover your nose and mouth to block viral particles.

setup.label: Setup
setup.title: How to get the best experience?
steps: Open chrome://flags and enable all WebAssembly features.
Restart Chrome, open this page, and allow camera access.
Safari on iOS is supported but may run at a lower frame rate.
setup.note: Frame rate depends on your device CPU.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.title: Privacy statement
privacy.body: Everything runs fully inside your browser via WebAssembly. No images or videos leave your device, and no data is stored on any server. You can even disconnect the internet once detection starts.

project.label: Project
project.title: Project overview
project.paragraph1: WearMask (Web-based Efficient AI Recognition of Masks) is a deep learning project based on Yolo-Fastest, trained with PyTorch, and deployed through NCNN and WebAssembly.
project.paragraph2: This project is open-sourced on GitHub (deployment) and GitHub (training). See the research page and paper (DOI).
project.disclaimer: WearMask is a research and demonstration system, not a medical device or diagnostic tool.

modal.title: Camera permission required
modal.body: To start mask detection, allow your browser to access the camera in its settings, then refresh this page.

aboutPage.title: About WearMask | In-browser Face Mask Detection
aboutPage.heading: WearMask: In-browser Face Mask Detection
aboutPage.intro: WearMask is an open-source, real-time face mask detection system that runs entirely inside a web browser. The project is also published as WearMask: Fast in-browser face mask detection with serverless edge computing for COVID-19.
aboutPage.q1_body: WearMask (Web-based Efficient AI Recognition of Masks) detects whether people in a webcam feed appear to be wearing a face mask. Unlike cloud-based vision services, all inference happens on the user's device. No camera images or video are uploaded to an application server.
aboutPage.q2_title: How is it different from cloud vision?
aboutPage.q2_item1: Privacy: Camera data never leaves the browser.
aboutPage.q2_item2: Serverless: No backend GPU or inference API is required.
aboutPage.q2_item3: Edge computing: Detection runs on the user's CPU via WebAssembly.
aboutPage.q2_item4: Open source: Deployment and training code are publicly available.
aboutPage.q3_title: What does fully local inference mean?
aboutPage.q3_body: After the page loads the WebAssembly model, detection runs on each video frame inside the browser. The application does not send images, video, or detection results to a WearMask server. You can disconnect from the internet after the model has loaded and detection will continue to work.
aboutPage.q4_author: Primary author: Zekun Wang (ORCID · LinkedIn)
aboutPage.q4_inst: Institution: Vanderbilt University Data Science Institute
aboutPage.q4_support: Research supported in part by the U.S. National Science Foundation.
aboutPage.q5_item1: First public release: November 2020 (browser demo and open-source code)
aboutPage.disclaimer: Important: WearMask is a research and demonstration system, not a medical device or diagnostic tool.

limitationsPage.title: Known Limitations
limitationsPage.subtitle: Important constraints regarding model accuracy, hardware performance, and intended usage scope.
limitationsPage.sec1_body: WearMask is built for research, education, and open-source technology demonstration. It is not certified as a medical device or health safety diagnostic tool.
limitationsPage.sec2_body: Detection accuracy depends on camera resolution, ambient lighting, face orientation, and extreme angles or severe occlusions.
limitationsPage.sec3_body: Because WebAssembly relies on client-side CPU execution, frame rates vary significantly across different mobile and desktop processors.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Statement
privacyPage.subtitle: How WearMask protects user privacy through complete client-side processing.
privacyPage.sec1_body: All image processing and AI inference happen locally inside your browser memory. No camera feeds or snapshot images leave your device.
privacyPage.sec2_body: Once the initial WebAssembly model file is cached, WearMask operates seamlessly without an active internet connection.

researchPage.title: Research Paper & Background
researchPage.subtitle: Academic details and publication info for WearMask.
researchPage.sec1_body: WearMask presents a lightweight, serverless edge computing framework for real-time face mask detection directly inside standard web browsers.
researchPage.pubInfo: Published in Electronic Imaging 2023 (High-Performance Computing and Artificial Intelligence Applications).

techPage.title: Technical Overview
techPage.subtitle: Architecture, models, and technologies driving WearMask.
techPage.sec1_body: WearMask combines YOLO-Fastest (lightweight object detection) with Tencent NCNN framework compiled into WebAssembly for high-speed client-side C++ execution.
techPage.sec2_body: Leverages WebAssembly SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) and multi-threading for fast real-time inference on modern CPUs.
